source.title: Energy-based characterization of sparse sensor interactions
source.authors: A. Klishin; J. Kutz; Krithika Manohar

record.file_problem: The text is a complete paper and supplementary materials. Its title differs from the supplied title, but the text is not cut off or garbled.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses double descent and reports reconstruction-risk curves for sparse sensor placement, but those are not results on the AI model classes or axes named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports sensor-reconstruction risk while varying sensor count, including peaks and their suppression with regularization. These are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of the claim versions. Double-descent results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own risk curves over sensor count in Bayesian sparse-sensor state reconstruction. It finds a peak at p≈r for least-squares or unregularized reconstruction and shows that POD-prior regularization removes it. Sensor count is the number of measurements used to infer r POD coefficients for one state. It is not model size, training epochs, or training-sample count for a learned model, and the system is a linear inverse problem rather than an ML model class. The curve is formally close to sample-wise double descent in linear regression, and regularization suppressing the peak resembles V6. Even so, the measured construct differs from what the versions name, so these results are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that regularized reconstruction suppresses the double-descent phenomenon in the sensor-placement context, with any peak occurring at sensor count ≈ mode count. They say they do not exhaustively explain risk-curve shapes across datasets and leave optimal regularization design to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies Bayesian regularized sparse-state reconstruction and sensor-count risk curves, rather than the original deep-network model-size or training-data experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction risk depends on the prior configuration: isotropic sensor placement with isotropic reconstruction only slightly suppresses the peak, while the other three tested prior combinations yield monotonic curves without a peak. The paper also reports different curve behavior across datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: In linear sparse-sensor reconstruction, least-squares or unregularized reconstruction error over sensor count peaks at p≈r (number of retained POD modes). Regularization with a POD prior removes the peak, while an isotropic prior for both placement and reconstruction only slightly suppresses it. Regularized curves are monotonic or nearly monotonic across datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In sparse-sensing reconstruction, risk over sensor count can peak where sensor count equals retained mode count, and Bayesian prior regularization suppresses or removes this peak.

record.peer_reviewed: Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering
record.problems: The double-descent-related results concern sparse sensing rather than the model settings in the claim. The authors state that the uncertainty estimates miss other error contributions and that the risk-curve shape is not exhaustively explained. Reported RMSE curves include uncertainty bands, but the text does not provide their numerical values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were omitted.

untested.parts: Training-sample count near an interpolation threshold for a learned model. Sensor count is only an analogue.
Capacity sweeps past interpolation across model classes.
An effective-complexity measure predicting the peak location.
Label-noise or variance as the driver of the peak, multiple descent, and optimally tuned regularization in model-learning settings. The paper does not tune regularization optimally.

record.verdict_notes: Borderline case. Reconstruction with p sensors and r unknowns is mathematically a linear regression with p observations, so the least-squares peak at p≈r parallels sample-wise double descent (V3), and its removal by a prior parallels V6. A curator who accepts sensor-measurement count as an analogue of sample count could reclassify as T3 with V3/V6 links (R7 observed, R8 partial, R9–R11 suppressed under non-tuned regularization). Under the stated rule (same behaviour, same kind of system), it is kept out of the versions. Two internal inconsistencies in the source are flagged under R1 and R2.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise double descent in deep networks.
Changing the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
Capacity sweeps across model classes and generalization risk past an interpolation point.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
Label-noise or variance as the cause of peaks, multiple or triple descent, and optimally tuned regularization in the claim's model settings.
Recounting complexity by effective parameter number to determine whether a second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.
